options: Any kind of unusual behaviour which can degrade the quality of data
Statistical outliers in a numeric column
Errors in a BI dashboard layout
Unused indexes in a database
Delays in a data pipeline
questions.explanation: Data Anomalies are about any kind of unusual behaviour which can degrade the quality of data, including being unable to insert, update or delete required data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of Data Anomalies listed?
options: Insertion
Update
Delete
Redundancy
Encryption
questions.explanation: The four types listed are Insertion, Update, Delete and Redundancy anomalies.

options: Being unable to enter quality data into a database
Being able to update irrelevant data
Having duplicate records in a table
Deleting a whole department by deleting an employee
Losing a backup copy
questions.explanation: Redundancy is when there are duplicate records in a table.

questions.stem: Which two practices play a vital role in making sure data anomalies do not occur?
options: Data visualisation and heat maps
Data Normalisation and database constraints
Data surfing and ad hoc reporting
Machine learning and deep learning
Hub-and-spoke and point-to-point integration
questions.explanation: Data Normalisation and database constraints play a vibrant role in making sure data anomalies do not occur.

questions.stem: In the de-normalised employee table example, a rule says department name cannot be NULL. What anomaly arises when a new employee has not yet been assigned a department?
options: A redundancy anomaly, because the employee is duplicated
A delete anomaly, because the department is removed
An update anomaly, because the salary changes
An insertion anomaly, because the employee record cannot be inserted and a report of all employees will be wrong
No anomaly, because the rule is correct
questions.explanation: The new employee's record cannot be inserted until a department is assigned, so a management report of all employees will be wrong, which is a data anomaly.

questions.stem: In the de-normalised employee table example, what happens when the only employee in the HR department is deleted?
options: The HR department details are deleted as well, so analysis shows no HR department exists
The salary column becomes NULL
A duplicate HR department record is created
The employee is moved to the IT department
The table is automatically normalised
questions.explanation: Deleting that employee record from the de-normalised table means deleting the HR department details as well, so at that point in time there would appear to be no HR department, which is a data anomaly.

questions.stem: In the employee table example, Adam has two departments, IT and Procurement. What update anomaly can occur when renaming IT to Tech Org?
options: Adam's salary is doubled
Adam's record is deleted
The update also changes Procurement to Tech Org, creating a data quality issue
The update is rejected by the database
A third department is added for Adam
questions.explanation: If one is unaware of Adam's multiple departments, an update command to change IT to Tech Org will also update Procurement to Tech Org, which is a data anomaly.

questions.stem: Besides eliminating duplication of records, what other benefit is gained by normalising the employee table into separate department and salary tables?
options: Faster network speed
Saving a lot of storage
Better dashboard colours
Automatic data encryption
Removal of all database constraints
questions.explanation: Splitting the employee table into department and salary tables eliminates duplication and redundancy, saves a lot of storage, and addresses the insert, update and delete anomalies.

questions.stem: Which statement about data quality is made in the discussion of Data Anomalies?
options: Data quality is only about dirty data
Data quality applies only to reports
Data quality is unaffected by database design
Data quality is measured only by row counts
Data quality is not only about dirty data but also about being unable to insert, update and delete required data
questions.explanation: Data quality is not only about dirty data but also about not being able to insert, update and delete required data.

questions.stem: How is an Update anomaly defined?
options: Being unable to enter quality data into a database
Having duplicate records in a table
Being able to delete irrelevant data
Being unable to update relevant data, or being able to update irrelevant data
Being unable to create a new table
questions.explanation: An Update anomaly is when one is unable to update relevant data or is able to update irrelevant data.
